# mmx-pri-1.2 — a Dwarf Priest who got to level 3, found 190 gold, and did not find a staircase

**Seed 17, class Priest (given), race drawn: Dwarf. 58 asks (148 to 205), 15,150
game turns. Maximum depth 1. Character level 3. Alive: stopped, saved, 33/33
hit points, 4/6 spell points, AC 9, 163 gold. No down staircase found, on this
level or on the fresh one that replaced it.**

This is the second life of the character `mmx-pri-1` stopped at character level
2 on depth 1 with 8 gold, 18 flasks of oil, no potion and no scroll. The
inheritance mattered: the first life had spent both Potions of Cure Serious
Wounds, the Scroll of Phase Door and the Scroll of Word of Recall, so **the
escape ladder arrived empty** and this life had to buy one back out of a town
it could only reach by finding the staircase it never found.

## What the life actually was

| | |
|---|---|
| Asked | 58 decisions, of which 5 were in the town and 2 were the M map |
| Level | 2 → 3 (four experience: a rock lizard, a soldier ant, a giant yellow centipede) |
| Killed | 3 monsters: a rock lizard, a soldier ant, a giant yellow centipede |
| Hurt | 9 hit points, all of it from one yellow mushroom patch; healed free with Minor Healing |
| Gold | 8 → 198 (two piles on the floor) → 163 after buying |
| Bought | a Scroll of Phase Door (15) and a Potion of Cure Light Wounds (20) at the Alchemist |
| Depth | 1, and the level it was found on was abandoned and replaced |

**The staircase was the whole shape of the run and it was not found.** The
first depth-1 level was covered to about 15 per cent of its 13,068 squares with
no `>` anywhere on the M map; the town was reached, the shops were read, and
the second depth-1 level — a different one, because a level you leave is gone —
was covered to 1 per cent before the run stopped. No Magic Mapping was for
sale, so there was no instrument that could have found one.

## What I measured, and what it is worth

**The status line's `Light N` is the light of the SQUARE, not of your torch.**
`ui-display.c` `prt_light()` prints `square_light(cave, player->grid)`. So
`Light 1` is a dim corridor, `Light 2` a lit corridor, `Light 3` an open room,
`Light 0` (in purple) is darkness, and the town shows `Light 1`. It rose and
fell twice in this run without my doing anything, and I spent asks wondering
why. **It is a free reading of whether the ground under you is a room or a
corridor** — which is the same thing the map tells you, only it works when the
map is scrolled away.

**Aiming at a KNOWN square walks a long way.** `*p` then 25 east and 16 north
then `g`, aimed at the up staircase I had drawn on my map, walked me 25 tiles
in **one ask** (ask 186). This is the one long-distance movement in the game
that works every time: the destination is known, so `find_path` sets
`only_known = true` and computes a real path over remembered ground. Aiming
into **unknown** ground is the opposite: in this run it moved me one tile and
printed `Target Aborted.` (ask 152). Every note in this family about the
aim-walk says the same thing from both sides, and this is the cleanest
measurement of the difference: 25 tiles against 1, in consecutive asks, with
the same key shape.

**A chain of direction digits is one ask, and it dies at the first wall.**
`cmd-cave.c` `do_cmd_walk_test()` calls `disturb()` when the square is a known
wall, and `disturb()` ends with `event_signal(EVENT_INPUT_FLUSH)`, which the
agent patch turns into "the rest of the string is dropped". So a chain of
twenty known-floor steps is one ask (ask 150: 10 west and 10 south in one ask)
and a chain that meets a wall halfway is one ask and one wall learned.

**Doors cost one key, and an open door is one key too.** Walking into a locked
door picks the lock and the pick repeats the walk, so one key opens it and
walks through (ask 173: `You have picked the lock.` and I was through).
Walking into an **open** door closes it, and the close repeats the walk, so
one key closes it, re-opens it and walks through. A door is never two asks.

**`l<g` and `l>g` are the two best keys in the game and they are one ask each.**
`l<g` parks the cursor on the nearest **known** up staircase and `g` walks
there over remembered ground (ask 185, 25 tiles in one ask to the staircase
I could see). `l>g` did the same in the town for the town's down staircase,
though it was interrupted twice by townfolk before it arrived.

**The Dwarf sees treasure veins three tiles away, every turn.**
`game-world.c` `process_player()` calls `effect_simple(EF_DETECT_ORE, ...)`
with radius 3,3 for anyone with the Dwarf's `SEE_ORE` flag, and
`effect_handler_DETECT_ORE` memorises the square. So a `*` on my map is a vein
I had not even stepped next to. The veins in this run were all plain `%`
(magma or quartz, no treasure), which is why digging never paid.

**Magic Mapping really does put a down staircase on the map.**
`effect_handler_MAP_AREA` memorises every **non-floor** feature in its window,
and a staircase is not floor. The window is the half-extents 22 by 40 of
`object.txt`, so 44 rows by 80 columns — 27 per cent of a level — and a level
has three or four staircases, so one scroll is a good bet. **But the Alchemist
did not have one.** The shop's `normal:` list is fourteen kinds and `slots:6:10`
fills six to ten of them a day, so a given normal is there about half the time;
on this seed, on day two, the Alchemist's list had no Magic Mapping, no
Monster Confusion and no Cure Serious Wounds, and it had gained Neutralize
Poison, Berserk Strength, Resist Heat, Resist Cold and Remove Hunger. The
stock **rotates**: the same shop, the same seed, the day before, had a
different list. Anyone who plans a shopping trip around one item is gambling
on the rotation, not on the shop.

**A yellow mushroom patch on depth 1 took 9 hit points and my attacks.**
The yellow mushroom patch is `depth:2` (`SPORE:TERRIFY:1d6`) and it was on a
depth-1 level — the game's own 1-in-25 chance of a monster from a deeper
level. Being afraid gave me **AC 17 instead of AC 9** (fear is worth eight
points of armour class, as `minimaxflash-1.5` measured) and I could not attack
while it lasted. The fear is a timer, not a condition you cure: it ran out
while I walked away, and the free cure is a Potion of Boldness (8 gold in the
Alchemist, which I did not buy). **Do not stand next to a mushroom patch, and
buy Boldness if you have to.**

## What I got wrong, which a next Priest should not

1. **The keypad, for the third time in this family.** I sent `6` meaning west
   and walked east into a wall (ask 149). `4` is west, `6` is east, `8` is
   north, `2` is south. My own playbook had this on it twice and I had it
   again. **Write the chain as words, then translate.**
2. **I spent 20 asks on the keypad of a staircase I was never going to find.**
   The first level's M map showed 6.4 per cent covered and no `>`; by the time
   I gave it up it was 8.9 per cent. Three or four staircases on 13,068
   squares means 15 per cent coverage has a chance of about half of one
   staircase, and **the answer was not more walking**. It was the town: the
   shop that restocks daily, and the one instrument (Magic Mapping) that can
   find a staircase without walking to it. I should have gone to the town at
   ask 152, not at ask 185.
3. **I read a `?` on the floor as a scroll.** The item at (10,12) was drawn
   `?` and it turned out to be a second Holy Book of Prayers, and my pack read
   `a) 2 Holy Books of Prayers [Novice's Handbook]`. `object.txt` gives scrolls
   `graphics:?:w`, but `object_base.txt` gives a prayer book only a colour
   ("light green"), so the symbol for a book is decided elsewhere and `?` does
   not mean a scroll here. **Look at an item before you plan around it.**
4. **I chased a second Novice's Handbook and a sword I did not need.** The
   Dagger on the floor at (33,16) throws for 1d4 x 6, which is worse than a
   flask of oil (9 to 36), and my blessed Mace already does 4 to 10. A
   Priest's second weapon is worth nothing. The spare book is worth 25 gold
   of carried value and nothing else.
5. **I never checked the Character sheet.** `CON` is the whole pace of this
   class, and I carried it in my head from the previous life instead of
   reading it off `C`.

## The leads, and what would settle each

1. **How much of a level does a run actually need to cover?** I covered 15 per
   cent of one level and 1 per cent of another in 58 asks, and found nothing.
   *What would settle it:* one run that spends its whole budget on the
   aim-walk at a known destination and on the `M` map, and reports the
   coverage after every ten asks with the number of staircases it had seen.
   The number I would like is the coverage at which the expected number of
   staircases seen passes one.
2. **Is the 'ood monster' chance the reason a depth-2 monster is on depth 1?**
   `mon-make.c` `get_mon_num()` boosts the generated depth by up to four
   levels one time in 25, and a yellow mushroom patch (`depth:2`) terrorised
   me on depth 1. *What would settle it:* a run that meets several depth-2
   monsters on depth 1 and counts them against the 1-in-25.
3. **Can a run find a down staircase at all on depth 1?** Nobody here has.
   The best evidence is `minimaxflash-3`, which found one at ask 85 after
   exploring 70 asks, and `minimaxflash-2.2`, which found one already
   remembered. *What would settle it:* one run that buys a Magic Mapping
   scroll the day the Alchemist has one, reads it on arrival, and says
   whether a `>` appears in the 44 by 80 window. My money is on that being
   worth more than every hour of walking I spent.

## What I would do differently

- **Go to the town early**, buy the Phase Door and the Cure Light Wounds
  before anything else, and read the Alchemist's list while you are there:
  the rotation is the one piece of information in this game that changes what
  is worth doing, and I read it with 20 asks left.
- **Sweep a level with aim-walks at KNOWN landmarks** — the staircase you
  arrived on, the far corner of a room you have lit — not with blind chains
  into the dark, which stop at the first wall and tell you one tile.
- **Buy a Potion of Boldness (8 gold) before you meet a mushroom patch.**
- **Keep the 18 flasks and do not carry a second weapon.** The Priest's
  problem on depth 1 is not damage output, it is that a mouse nest is a tax
  of one to two hit points on every ask, and 18 flasks plus a corridor is
  enough to get through it.

## The lead I did not take

The first life ended with 8 gold and an empty escape ladder. This life ended
with 163 gold, a Phase Door, a Cure Light Wounds, 33 of 33 hit points and
character level 3, **and it still did not reach depth 2**. The honest summary
is that a Priest without a staircase is a very slow character: every kill is
one to two experience at level 2 and one to two-thirds at level 3, and the
level's sixteen to twenty-four monsters are spread over thirteen thousand
squares. The run was bought, not earned: the gold and the two supplies are
what I have to show for fifty-eight decisions.
